title: Content as Structure: Why 4,700 Images Are Worth Less Than 20 Frameworks
lede: We hold 4,547 outfit images and 1,587 structured game suits. Here is the uncomfortable truth: the images are the cheap part. The frameworks derived from them are the asset.
body_md:
## The uncomfortable arithmetic
We hold 4,547 outfit images and 1,587 structured game suits. The images took years of collection. The 20 frameworks derived from them took 68 controlled experiments — and those frameworks are the only part competitors cannot copy.

## Why images are cheap
Images are reproducible by any scraper with an API. Google indexes them by the billion. A visitor who sees a pretty image has no reason to return — the next site has prettier ones.

## Why structure is expensive
A framework like '20 Failure Modes' requires: collect images → identify patterns → isolate variables → run experiments → codify. Each step is human judgment that cannot be shortcut by scraping.

## The compounding effect
Images deprecate (platforms change, links rot — we just removed six dead ones). Frameworks compound: every new experiment either confirms or refines an existing rule. The library grows more valuable with use.

## What we decided
Our site positioning follows this arithmetic: not 'more images' but 'more structure per image'. Every collection has a curator note; every topic has a formula; every deep article has a named framework.

## Related
The Economy of AI Reference Images covers the cost side; the Methodology Lab is the result.
